questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a piece of work in 6 days, 12 days and 15 days, respectively. P starts working alone on 1st, 4th, 7th... Q works alone on 2ⁿd, 5th, 8th and R works alone on 3rd, 6th, 9th... This pattern is continued till the work is completed. In how much time (in days) is the entire work done?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Work done by P in 1 day = 1/6

Work done by Q in 1 day = 1/12

Work done by R in 1 day = 1/15

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Sum of work done by P, Q, and R in the given pattern

**Calculation:**

LCM of 6, 12, and 15 is 60.

Work done by P on 1st day = 60/6 = 10

Work done by Q on 2ⁿd day = 60/12 = 5

Work done by R on 3rd day = 60/15 = 4

Total work done in 3 days = 10 + 5 + 4 = 19

⇒ Work done in 9 days work = 19 × 3 = 57 units

⇒ Total work left = 60 - 57 = 3

⇒ Time taken to complete 3 units of work by P = 3/10

⇒ Total time = 9 + 3/10 = 9(3)/(10) days.

**The correct answer is 9(3)/(10) days**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 10 hours and 13(1)/(3) hours, respectively. Pipe C is an emptying pipe. When all the three pipes are opened together, the tank is filled in 8 hours. In how many hours will Pipe C alone empty 25% of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Part filled by Pipe A in 1 hour = 1over10

Part filled by Pipe B in 1 hour = 1over{13{1over3}} = 3over40 

⇒ Total part filled by A and B working together in 1 hour = 1over10 + 3over40 = 7over40

Let the Pipe empty 1over c part in 1 hour.

When all opened together-

⇒ 7over40 - 1over c = 1over 8

⇒ 1over c = 7over40 - 1over 8

⇒ 1over c = 7-5over40

⇒ 1over c = 2over 40

⇒ c = 20 hours

Time required by the Pipe C alone to empty 25% of the tank

⇒ 0.25 × 20 = 5 hours.

**∴ Pipe C would require 5 hours to empty the tank alone.**

questions.question: Five technicians of a Studio A can do a work in 30 days. Eight technicians of a Studio B can do the same work in 15 days. In how many days can one technician of Studio A and one technician of Studio B, together do the same work?
questions.solution:
Number of technicians × studio A × days = Number of technicians × studio B × days

⇒ 5 × studio A × 30 = 8 × studio B × 15

⇒ 5 × studio A = 4 × studio B

⇒ Studio A/Studio B = 4/5

⇒ Time taken by one technician of studio A and one technician of studio B together to complete the work = (5 × 4 × 30)/(4 + 5)

⇒ Time taken by one technician of studio A and one technician of studio B together to complete the work = 200/3 days

∴ Total work will be done by one technician of studio A and one technician of studio B together in 200/3 days.

⇒ R + P + Q = 1/70

∴ R, P and Q can complete the work in 70 days

questions.question: X takes 10 days less than the time taken by Y to finish a piece of work. X and Y together can do it in 12 days. In how many days Y-alone can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Let the time taken by Y to finish the work be a days

⇒ The time taken by X to finish the work is (a – 10) days

⇒ The work done by Y in 1 day = 1/a

And, the work done by X in 1 day = 1/(a – 10)

According to question,

1/a + 1/(a – 10) = 1/12

⇒ (2a – 10)/(a² – 10a) = 1/12

⇒ a² – 10a = 24a – 120

⇒ a² – 34a + 120 = 0

⇒ (a – 30) (a – 4) = 0

So, a = 30 or a = 4 (which is not possible)

∴ Y can alone finish the work in 30 days

questions.question: Aadish can complete a work in 14 days. If he worked for 8 days, then what fraction of the work would be left?

The fraction of work left is given by the number of days left divided by the total number of days.

questions.question: A and B working together can complete a job in 90 days. The ratio of their efficiencies is 3 ∶ 5. In how many days can the faster person complete the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(A + B)'s time to complete the job = 90 days

Efficiency ratio of A to B = 3:5

**Formula:**

Time taken is inversely proportional to efficiency.

**Solution: **

⇒ A's efficiency = 3 parts, B's efficiency = 5 parts

⇒ Total 8 parts are equal to A + B's work in 1 day.

⇒ Hence, 1 part is equal to (A + B)'s work / 8 in 1 da
y.

⇒ Therefore, B's one-day work (as he is faster) = 5 parts = 5 × (A + B)'s work / 8

⇒ So, B completes the work in 8/(5 × (A + B)'s work) days = 8/(5 × 1/90) days = 144 days

**Therefore, the faster person (B) can complete the job in 144 days.**

questions.question: A can complete (3)/(8) of a certain work in 9 days and B can complete 80% of the same work in 16 days. Both work together for 5 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 6 (1)/(2) days. A and C together will complete the whole work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete (3)/(8) of a work in 9 days

B can complete 80% of the work in 16 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Time required by A to complete the work = 9over {3over8} = 9 × 8over3 = 24 days

Time required by B to complete the work = 16over {80over100} = 16 × 100over80 = 20 days

Let the total work be 120 units (LCM of 24, 20)

Efficiency of A = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day

Efficiency of B = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 units/day

Combined efficiency of A and B = 5 + 6 = 11 units/day

Work done by A and B in 5 days = 11 × 5 = 55 units

Remaining work = 120 - 55 = 65 units or 65over120 part of the work

According to the question

65over120 part of the work is done by C in 6 (1)/(2) days

Time required by C to complete the total work

⇒ {13over2}over {65over120} = 13over 2 × 120over65 = 12 days

Efficiency of C = 120 ÷ 12 = 10 units/day

Combined efficiency of A and C = 5 + 10 = 15 units/day

Time taken by A and C to complete the work = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 days

**∴ A and C would complete the work in 8 days.**

questions.question: A alone can paint a house in 35 days and B alone can do it in 70 days. Along with C, they did the job in 10 days only. In how many days C alone can do the job?
questions.solution:

1 day’s work of A = 1/35

1 day’s work of B = 1/70

Let C alone can do the painting job in x days

According to the question,

⇒ 1/35+ 1/70 + 1/x = 1/10

⇒ 1/x = 1/10 - 3/70 = 4/70

⇒ x = 70/4

**∴ C alone can do the painting job in __70/4__ days.**

questions.question: A can build up a wall in 8 days while B can break it in 3 days. A has worked for 4 days, and then B joined to work with A for another 2 days only. In how many days will A alone build up the remaining part of the wall?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can build up a wall in 8 days.

B can break the wall in 3 days.

A has worked for 4 days alone.

B joined A for another 2 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/8

Work done by B in 1 day = -1/3

Remaining work = Total work - Work already done

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 4 days = 4 × 1/8

⇒ Work done by A in 4 days = 4/8 = 1/2

Remaining work after A has worked for 4 days = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2

Combined work done by A and B in 1 day = 1/8 - 1/3

⇒ Combined work done by A and B in 1 day = 3/24 - 8/24 = -5/24

Work done by A and B in 2 days = 2 × (-5/24)

⇒ Work done by A and B in 2 days = -10/24 = -5/12

Remaining work after A and B worked for 2 days = 1/2 - (-5/12)

⇒ Remaining work = 1/2 + 5/12 = 6/12 + 5/12 = 11/12

Time taken by A to build the remaining work = (Remaining work) / (Work done by A in 1 day)

⇒ Time taken by A = (11/12) / (1/8)

⇒ Time taken by A = 11/12 × 8/1

⇒ Time taken by A = 88/12

⇒ Time taken by A = 22/3 days

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of A and B is 5 ∶ 11. Working together, they can do the same work in 27(1)/(2) days. A and B work together for 20 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 18 days. C alone can do 75% of the original work in:

Working together, they can do the same work in 27(1)/(2) days i.e. {55 over 2} days

C alone completes the remaining work in 18 days

Total work = Work done each day × Total time taken (in days)

So, A and B do each day 5Q & 11Q units respectively.

Thus, total work = {55 over 2} × (5Q + 11Q) = 440Q units

Now, work done in 20 days by A and B together = (5Q + 11Q) × 20 = 320Q units

Remaining work = 440Q - 320Q = 120Q

Hence, efficiency of C = 120Q ÷ 18 = {20Q over 3} units

Thus, C alone can do 75% of the original work in = (440Q × 75%) ÷ {20Q over 3} = 49(1)/(2) days

**∴ C alone can do 75% of the original work in 49(1)/(2) days.**

questions.question: A, B, C work one after the other in that order. Each can finish a work individually in 10, 16, 12 days, respectively. After working for 3 such cycles ABC, ABC, ABC, then A and C leave the work. B alone will complete the rest of the work in:

 Rightarrow (177)/(240) 

Remaining work = 1 - (177 / 240)

 Rightarrow (240 - 177)/(240) 

 Rightarrow (63)/(240)

questions.question: Anit can do a piece of work in 77 days. Ram can do the same work in 11 days. Ram and Anit start working together but Ram left the work 3 days before the completion of the work. Find the approximate number of days in which the work is completed.

questions.question: F alone can complete a work in 24 days and G alone can complete the same work in 32 days. F and G start the work together but G leaves the work 8 days before the completion of work. In how many days the total work will be completed?

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task (Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time).

Total Work Concept

Total work is universally considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given number of days. This prevents complicated fractions and keeps efficiency values as simple integers.
